feature_notes.campaign x emp_var_rate_sigmoid_slope: Lost in drop_second; kept by the other candidates with the same pattern. Repeated contacts (campaign 6 and above) at emp.var.rate slopes of 0.487 (October-November 2008) and 0.559 (March-May 2009 and 2010) score from about -0.4 down to -0.67 (sandbox fit) or -0.62 (Windows fit) log-odds beyond the main effects; at higher slopes such cells are sparse. Fold sd at most about 0.06 in well-supported cells.
feature_notes.decay_x_density: Rises from about -0.1 at zero density (2008 rows, 21,991 in the lowest grid bin) to a plateau of +0.6 to +1.3 and falls below 0 above 0.13 (sparse, 2010). Fold 0 departs from the others everywhere: -2.2 at zero and +1.1 to +2.0 above it, against -0.7 to -0.2 and -0.1 to +1.1. Fold sd over well-supported values 0.513, the largest of any term; this is the fold-0 regime-step excursion.
feature_notes.decay_x_density_past: Not monotone: -0.58 at zero past density, +0.76 just above it, down to +0.18 at 0.008 to 0.010, then rising to +1.25 at 0.116 and falling to +0.92; 5 direction changes over well-supported values and the folds disagree most at low values (0.01 to 0.82). The 917 held-out rows contacted on days 0-2 have no raw value and carry their fold's fit-side median (about 2.8e-06), a fallback that depends on later labels.
feature_notes.emp_var_rate_sigmoid_slope: Values up to 0.058 score -0.1 to -0.2 and the rest +0.1 to +0.3. Fold 0 gives a larger step (0.34 vs 0.17 in the other folds) in the baseline and again in drop_first (0.37 vs 0.20), so removing the euribor slope does not remove it. In jed_alone the top value (0.99) turns negative. Most stable in past_density (fold sd 0.016).
feature_notes.euribor3m_sigmoid_slope: A two-regime step: -0.12 to -0.26 for the 2008 rows (slope below 0.04, 21,971 rows), rising from -0.20 at 0.53 to about +0.1 between 0.73 and 0.93 and +0.33 at the top value (2009-10). The fold models agree on direction, not on the step's size (0.06 to 0.32 log-odds), and disagree most at the two ends (-0.35 to +0.05 at the lowest value, +0.11 to +0.56 at the top). Re-centring over well-supported values moves a fold curve by at most 0.0085 (the five shifts span 0.0135) and leaves their spread unchanged, so the apparent offset is a shape difference, not a centring artefact. 8 of 12 well-supported points are single-period.
feature_notes.euribor3m_sigmoid_slope x economic_curva: Lost in drop_first. Within its 44 well-supported cells the effect is at most about 0.05 log-odds (0.048 in the sandbox fit, 0.051 in the Windows fit) while the fold sd reaches about 0.2: noise-level.
feature_notes.joint_economic_decay: A monotone rise in three levels: -0.13 to -0.04 for the 2008 rows (values up to 0.036), +0.47 to +0.66 for 0.07 to 0.09, and +0.75 to +1.09 for 0.32 to 0.39. The fold curves stay close (fold sd 0.085). Label-free: its only inputs are the three macro series.
feature_notes.prior_x_stress x decay_x_density: Lost in jed_alone and past_density. At most about 0.07 log-odds in a well-supported cell (0.068 in the sandbox fit, 0.072 in the Windows fit); in the sandbox fit the largest is -0.07 at prior_x_stress 0.42 to 0.67 with decay_x_density 0.0074 to 0.0075 (577 rows).

drop_first.rationale: Removes euribor3m_sigmoid_slope, the less stable of the two correlated regime slopes (r 0.725): its fold models disagree on the size of its 2009-10 vs 2008 step (sd 0.12 log-odds, 0.06 to 0.32) and 8 of its 12 well-supported grid points are single-period; in the baseline the two slopes split that step differently from fold to fold (their five per-fold steps correlate at -0.47: descriptive, consistent with the two slopes sharing one regime signal). Also drops euribor3m_sigmoid_slope x economic_curvature_intensity, at most about 0.05 log-odds in any well-supported cell (0.048 in the sandbox fit, 0.051 in the Windows fit) while its fold sd reaches about 0.2 there. 12 features, 2 pairs, one empty slot. Cost inside the tolerances: ROC-AUC -0.0004 (95% CI -0.0009 to 0.0002), PR-AUC -0.0018, nested F2 +0.0004, calibrated ECE 0.0018. It leaves decay_x_density's fold-0 excursion in place (period-level step sd 0.75 vs 0.63).

drop_second.rationale: Removes emp_var_rate_sigmoid_slope, the more stable of the two slopes (step sd 0.077 vs 0.119), and with it campaign x emp_var_rate_sigmoid_slope, the TIER 1 pair and the only retained pair with a substantive well-supported effect (0.81 to 0.87 log-odds across its supported cells in the two platforms' fits, fold sd at most about 0.06). The kept euribor slope keeps its fold disagreement (step sd 0.11). ROC-AUC -0.0013 (95% CI -0.0023 to -0.0003, p 0.011): inside the tolerance, but the only interval that excludes zero.

jed_alone.rationale: Replaces the label-derived decay_x_density (joint decay x NSD) with its label-free macro factor joint_economic_decay (r 0.9935). The slot's fold sd over well-supported values falls from 0.513 to 0.085 log-odds, and the period-level regime step agrees across folds (sd 0.064 vs 0.632; the baseline's fold 0 put 2.75 log-odds on it against 1.1 to 1.6, through decay_x_density alone). Loses prior_x_stress x decay_x_density, at most about 0.07 log-odds in any well-supported cell (0.068 sandbox, 0.072 Windows). 13 features, 2 pairs, one empty slot. Performance unchanged: ROC-AUC +0.0001 (95% CI -0.0004 to 0.0005), PR-AUC +0.0006, nested F2 +0.0010. Trade-offs: calibrated ECE 0.0027 vs 0.0019 (gate 0.05), and emp_var_rate_sigmoid_slope's top value (0.99, 519 rows) now scores -0.61 in the all-rows fit (fold models -0.13 to -0.44), part of the late-2010 decline decay_x_density carried.

past_density.rationale: More stable than the baseline (slot fold sd 0.172 vs 0.513; period-level step sd 0.071) and inside the tolerances (ROC-AUC +0.0005, 95% CI -0.0005 to 0.0014; PR-AUC +0.0017; nested F2 -0.0011 with the widest fold spread, sd 0.0087), but not easier to explain: its shape changes direction 5 times over well-supported values (joint_economic_decay 2), and the feature keeps a label-dependent kernel with a history state and a lag-0 outcome assumption. It is also not fully past-only: the 917 held-out rows contacted on days 0-2 take a fallback computed over the whole fit fold, and flipping a tenth of the later fit labels raises that fallback 3.1- to 3.6-fold and, with the fitted fold models held fixed, those rows' term score by 0.07 to 0.16 log-odds. joint_economic_decay reaches the same stability with no labels. Its case is temporal validity, which PR 49 tests once its fallback uses earlier data only; it is not carried into Step 5B reselection.

limits: Training side only, random outer folds. A simplification's value under a chronological split is PR 49's question; the past-only density changes only that one feature's construction.

The baseline is refitted from the tracked settings: the learning rate is transcribed to six decimals from glass_cascade Cell 18 (the only tracked source) and the sandbox runs Linux, not the accepted Windows environment. Parity is reported against the PR 39 records and, where the accepted artifact is available, row by row. Every candidate is compared with the refitted baseline, not with the artifact.

Each difference measures the whole simplification. Removing a feature also removes its pair; replacing decay_x_density also removes prior_x_stress x decay_x_density. Neither part is isolated, and no pair is reselected (Step 5B).
No candidate is retuned. The accepted hyperparameters were chosen for the 13-feature, three-pair model; a candidate's own optimum may differ.

The past-only density assumes an outcome is known by the next contact day (Step 3B's lag-0 rule); the outcome time is not recorded. Its history is grown, not redrawn. Its raw values are past-only; its fallback is not: rows without a raw value (917 held-out rows, contact days 0-2; 726-740 fit rows per fold; 4,374 inner held-out rows) get the production cleaner's median over the whole fit fold, which depends on labels of later contacts (fallback_trace). The candidate is evaluated as registered and fitted; a deployable version needs a fallback fixed from earlier data only.
The global raw and calibrated thresholds are chosen on the same rows they are applied to (in-selection); the fold-nested thresholds are the strictly nested operating point.

Shapes are fold models' and an all-rows fit's term scores on a common grid, each centred on the training rows. Sparse and single-period regions are marked, not removed; a period concentrated in a narrow range is evidence only there. For a period-level feature most values belong to one contact period, so a shape point is evidence about that period; the regime step compares periods.

Two presentation choices were made after the registered figures were inspected and change no fit, metric, threshold or ranking: pair surfaces are drawn on support-defined cells (the registered grid of both features left almost every cell empty, so its colour scale was set by unsupported extrapolation), and the fold offsets of the correlated slopes are re-examined by the centring check. The registered centring stays the reported one. The main-effect grid keeps every distinct value as registered, so two emp_var_rate_sigmoid_slope values equal up to floating-point noise appear as separate grid points.

Values that come from fitted models differ slightly between platforms (the sandbox's Linux fits and the accepted Windows run's): the pooled metrics in the last digits, the shape and pair summaries by up to about 0.05 log-odds (the TIER 1 pair's largest cell 0.671 vs 0.620, about its own fold spread). Data-determined quantities (rows, folds, cells, support, the fallback rows) are identical. The document's pair sizes are therefore stated for both platforms and checked as claims, not as third-decimal values.
The interpretability judgements (INTERPRETATION) are written after the results were seen; the registered rule asks for a documented gain, not a threshold, and the evidence for each is in the record.

Complementarity uses the accepted Stage 1 and Stage 2 decisions and is computed only where their artifacts exist locally. A disagreement count does not establish a better cascade decision; PRs 44-45 compare cascades at comparable coverage under the shared obligations.
Every target-dependent encoder (NSD, ECI, day x month) uses labels of later contacts under the accepted protocol (Commit 3); only the past-only candidate removes that for one feature.

definition.accepted: neighborhood_subscription_density: a Gaussian kernel average (bandwidth 1.0) of the fit rows' labels in standardized (euribor3m, nr.employed, emp.var.rate) space; the scaler is fitted on the fit rows; above 10,000 fit rows the reference is a 5,000-row draw (default_rng(42)); a fit row's own label is in its own value
definition.cold_start: a row has a value only from the first contact day at which its context's history holds at least 500 rows and 10 positives, and never on the first 3 contact days; earlier rows are missing and the production FeatureCleaner imputes them with the fit rows' median, as for every Stage 3 column. The missing rows are counted per context
definition.contexts: outer fold k: its fit rows (values for its fit rows and its held-out rows); inner fold j of fold k: the inner fit rows. A held-out row's value never uses another held-out row's label
definition.other_inputs: joint_economic_decay is a deterministic function of the current macro values
definition.outcome_availability: assumption (Step 3B's primary rule, lag 0): the outcome of a contact is known by the next contact day. Feasibility at prediction time depends on it; the outcome time is not recorded
definition.past_only: for a row contacted on day d (Commit 3 contact days), the same kernel average over the context's rows contacted on a day before d, with the scaler fitted on those rows and every one of them in the reference (the history is grown, not redrawn: Step 3B left this design choice open). Same-day labels are never used
definition.verification: on sampled days of one context, the production IntegralFeatureEngineer fitted on exactly the available rows (n_ref = their count, so no subsample) gives the same values

fallback_trace.description: The past-only candidate's final feature, decay_x_density_past, reaches the EBM in two forms. A row with a raw past-only density gets joint_economic_decay x that density, computed from labels of its context's rows contacted on earlier days only. A row without one (the first three contact days, or a history under 500 rows or 10 positives) gets the production FeatureCleaner's fallback: the median of decay_x_density_past over the whole fit side of its fold, whose values use labels of contacts up to the fold's last day. The fallback is therefore not past-only for the row it fills. The trace verifies both forms in the frames the EBM is fitted on and scores, counts the held-out rows that get the fallback, and flips fit-side labels contacted on or after the first held-out day with a raw value (a tenth of them, then all). Those contacts come after every fallback row's day, and no raw value up to that day can use them, so the raw values of that first valued day are a control that must not move; the question is whether the fallback does.

post_registration: accepted views checked before any fit: a present artifact that fails its pin or boundary check (or the training rows' labels) raises with its role; PR42_REQUIRE_ACCEPTED_VIEWS=1 requires all three and the reconciled complementarity tables (complementarity_requirement)

complementarity.availability: computed only where the accepted Stage 1 LR, GLASS router and EBM artifacts exist locally, through the boundary extractors; otherwise reported as unavailable
complementarity.comparison: Stage 1 errors the EBM corrects (EBM only correct) and correct Stage 1 decisions it overturns (Stage 1 only correct); net = corrected - overturned
complementarity.counts: both correct, Stage 1 only correct, EBM only correct, both wrong, with denominators, for all rows and for abstentions; each table must add up to its population
complementarity.decisions: Stage 1: lr.in_stage_f2_cv (calibrated LR out-of-fold probability >= its stored threshold); the accepted EBM: ebm.nested_f2 (stored decisions); refitted EBMs: raw out-of-fold score >= their own fold-nested threshold (the same rule). Correct = decision equals the label
complementarity.limit: a disagreement count does not establish a better cascade decision
complementarity.population: all training rows with out-of-fold outputs, aligned by row identity; Stage 2 abstentions = the accepted GLASS router's out-of-fold 'uncertain' rows

correlated_pair.order: first and second member in EBM_FEATURES order
correlated_pair.rule: the frozen inventory's pruning note names euribor3m_sigmoid_slope and emp_var_rate_sigmoid_slope (|r| = 0.724). Verified on the training rows: on the full-train block and on every outer fit side it must be the only pair of the 13 features with |Pearson r| >= 0.7. Otherwise the run stops (the registration would need a revision)

evaluation.folds: the baseline's outer and inner plans for every candidate
evaluation.isolation: features refitted inside each fold by the production pipeline; the past-only density is fold-isolated and contact-ordered; calibration and thresholds fold-nested

content.known_before_registration: The baseline refit (no candidate) was run once in the sandbox to check parity against the PR 39 records: its global raw F2 threshold equals the record's (0.53); its out-of-fold ECE before and after calibration, its calibrated threshold and three of its five fold-nested thresholds differ slightly (Linux against the accepted Windows run, and a learning rate transcribed to six decimals). No candidate feature set was fitted, and no candidate out-of-fold statistic computed, before this registration was fixed.

nomination.cascade: a candidate meeting those tolerances is nominated for later cascade evaluation if, on Stage 2 abstentions, its net count is at least the baseline's net count minus 0.5% of the abstention rows (computed only where the accepted artifacts are available locally)
nomination.modest_loss: a simpler model may advance with a loss inside these tolerances when the interpretability gain and calibration trade-off are documented
nomination.step5b: a candidate is recommended for Step 5B reselection if its paired ROC-AUC difference is >= -0.005 with a 95% lower bound >= -0.01, its PR-AUC difference >= -0.01, its nested F2 difference >= -0.01, its calibrated ECE <= 0.05 and its calibrated Brier <= the baseline's + 0.002, and its shapes give a documented interpretability gain

parity.records: the refitted baseline's out-of-fold ECE before and after calibration, global raw and calibrated thresholds and fold-nested thresholds against the PR 39 Commit 4 run record and the Commit 6 reproduction record (training side)
parity.row_aligned: where the accepted EBM artifact exists locally, read through shared.stage2.diagnostics.boundary.extract_ebm_view at its pinned SHA-256: raw and calibrated out-of-fold scores and stored nested decisions, row by row (maximum absolute difference, correlation, ROC-AUC difference, decisions that differ)
parity.use: descriptive, and explained where it differs. Every candidate is compared with the refitted baseline (same code, platform, settings), never with the accepted artifact's vectors

past_only_density.accepted: neighborhood_subscription_density: a Gaussian kernel average (bandwidth 1.0) of the fit rows' labels in standardized (euribor3m, nr.employed, emp.var.rate) space; the scaler is fitted on the fit rows; above 10,000 fit rows the reference is a 5,000-row draw (default_rng(42)); a fit row's own label is in its own value
past_only_density.cold_start: a row has a value only from the first contact day at which its context's history holds at least 500 rows and 10 positives, and never on the first 3 contact days; earlier rows are missing and the production FeatureCleaner imputes them with the fit rows' median, as for every Stage 3 column. The missing rows are counted per context
past_only_density.contexts: outer fold k: its fit rows (values for its fit rows and its held-out rows); inner fold j of fold k: the inner fit rows. A held-out row's value never uses another held-out row's label
past_only_density.other_inputs: joint_economic_decay is a deterministic function of the current macro values
past_only_density.outcome_availability: assumption (Step 3B's primary rule, lag 0): the outcome of a contact is known by the next contact day. Feasibility at prediction time depends on it; the outcome time is not recorded
past_only_density.past_only: for a row contacted on day d (Commit 3 contact days), the same kernel average over the context's rows contacted on a day before d, with the scaler fitted on those rows and every one of them in the reference (the history is grown, not redrawn: Step 3B left this design choice open). Same-day labels are never used
past_only_density.verification: on sampled days of one context, the production IntegralFeatureEngineer fitted on exactly the available rows (n_ref = their count, so no subsample) gives the same values

content.question: Can the frozen PR 39 Stage 3 EBM be simplified so its contributions are easier to explain and more stable across folds and contact periods? What does each simplification gain or cost in out-of-fold predictive performance, calibration and its ability to correct Stage 1 mistakes, especially on rows where Stage 2 abstains?

shapes.grid: 60 points between the 0.5% and 99.5% quantiles of the full-train block values, or every value for a feature with at most 30 distinct values; the same grid for a feature in every model
shapes.interactions: each retained pair's term score on a grid of both features (all-rows fit), with joint row support; one symmetric colour scale per pair across models

shapes.periods: rows per contact period per bin; a bin whose largest period holds more than 50% of its rows is a single-period region

shapes.units: main effects in the EBM's additive term score (log-odds); the calibrated probability is a separate quantity and is never plotted as a term

scope: PR 42 Commit 5 Step 5A: feature analysis and Stage 3 EBM simplification (training side; standalone Stage 3 and its relationship to Stage 1 and Stage 2 decisions)

centring_check.description: Post-registration check, added after the shape figures were inspected; it changes no fit, metric, threshold or ranking. The fold curves of the correlated slopes look vertically offset. Under the registered centring every curve has mean 0 over all training rows. Here each fold curve is re-centred over the rows in well-supported bins only (support bins holding at least SPARSE_SHARE of the rows, inside the plotted range); each fold's shift is reported, with their largest absolute value (how far any fold curve moves) and their range across folds (how far the curves move relative to one another). Two centring-free quantities are taken per fold: the curve's amplitude (max - min) over those rows, and its regime step (mean contribution of the 2009-2010 rows minus that of the 2008 rows). The step is also taken for the sum of the two slopes, for the sum of every period-level main term (features constant within a contact day up to floating-point noise), for that sum without the decay slot (decay_x_density or its replacement) and for the whole additive score, to separate disagreement about the regime effect from disagreement about how it is split between correlated terms. With five folds the correlation of the two slopes' steps is descriptive only (no test).
